variants.title: Build the review path
variants.context: A review request must preserve enough evidence to reproduce the decision. The case is created at inference with the model output and policy context, assigned to a queue that matches domain, risk, and deadline, resolved with a reasoned decision, then closed with owner, timestamps, rationale, and policy version.
variants.prompt: A prediction crosses the escalation boundary and a reviewer must handle it. Put the case steps in order.

items.text: Capture a reasoned decision that supports approve, correct, abstain, and escalate without forcing a false answer.
Close and audit by recording the final owner, timestamps, rationale, policy version, and downstream side effect.
Create the case by persisting the model output and policy context before acknowledging that review was requested.
Assign the queue by matching domain, language, risk, and deadline to a reviewer with the required permissions.

variants.hint: What has to be durable before the caller is told a person will look at this?
variants.explanation: Persisting the output and policy context first is what makes the decision reproducible later, so the acknowledgement never outruns the record.

variants.title: Build the review path
variants.context: A review request must preserve enough evidence to reproduce the decision. The case is created at inference with the model output and policy context, assigned to a queue that matches domain, risk, and deadline, resolved with a reasoned decision, then closed with owner, timestamps, rationale, and policy version.
variants.prompt: An auditor six months later must reconstruct why one case was decided as it was. Put the steps that produced that record in order.

items.text: The queue assignment recorded which permissions and deadline the case required.
The reviewer's action and written rationale were attached to the same case ID.
The closing record added the final owner, timestamps, policy version, and the side effect that was applied.
The input reference, prediction, confidence signals, routing rule version, and model version were stored under one durable case ID.

variants.hint: Follow the case ID from creation to closure.
variants.explanation: One durable case ID carries evidence from every stage, which is what lets an audit reproduce the decision instead of re-guessing it.

variants.title: Build the review path
variants.context: A review request must preserve enough evidence to reproduce the decision. The case is created at inference with the model output and policy context, assigned to a queue that matches domain, risk, and deadline, resolved with a reasoned decision, then closed with owner, timestamps, rationale, and policy version.
variants.prompt: A general reviewer opens a case, finds it policy-sensitive, and escalates instead of answering. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The case is reassigned to a specialist queue whose reviewers hold the required permissions.
The reviewer chooses escalate rather than forcing an answer, and records why.
The case is assigned to the general review queue that its original risk tier called for.
The case closes with both owners, both timestamps, and the policy version that governed the escalation.
The case is created at inference with its prediction, uncertainty signals, and routing rule version.

variants.hint: Escalating is a first-class decision option, not a failure to decide.
variants.explanation: A review interface that offers approve, correct, abstain, and escalate keeps reviewers from inventing answers, and the audit record keeps both owners.

variants.title: Separate the two loops
variants.context: A HITL system runs two loops. The decision loop resolves the current case: the model predicts, a policy routes, and a person decides. The learning loop turns validated past decisions into a candidate model, so feedback crosses a quality gate before it can influence any future version.
variants.prompt: One case moves from a prediction to a future model version. Put the stages in order.

items.text: A candidate is retrained, evaluated by slice, canaried, and monitored before wider promotion.
The model returns a prediction with calibrated uncertainty, reason signals, and its version.
The policy routes the case by combining confidence with risk, novelty, policy rules, and available capacity.
The feedback is validated: agreement is measured, disputes resolved, leakage removed, and labels versioned.
The reviewer approves, corrects, rejects, escalates, or abstains with a recorded rationale.

variants.hint: Which stage stands between a click and a training set?
variants.explanation: The learning gate is what stops the system from learning directly from every click, because reviewer error and selection bias have to be measured first.

variants.title: Separate the two loops
variants.context: A HITL system runs two loops. The decision loop resolves the current case: the model predicts, a policy routes, and a person decides. The learning loop turns validated past decisions into a candidate model, so feedback crosses a quality gate before it can influence any future version.
variants.prompt: A reviewer corrects a wrong prediction. Put the steps that let that correction reach a model in order.

items.text: Agreement is measured and disagreements are adjudicated before any label is called authoritative.
The feedback pipeline samples the completed case alongside audit and stratified cases.
A candidate model is trained on that dataset and evaluated against stable holdouts and protected slices.
The correction is recorded with its rationale against the durable case ID.
The candidate runs in shadow and a bounded canary before it takes broad traffic.
Leakage is removed and the authoritative label is written into a versioned dataset.

variants.hint: A single correction is evidence, not truth.
variants.explanation: Corrections become authoritative labels only after sampling, agreement measurement, adjudication, and versioning, which is what keeps reviewer mistakes out of the model.

variants.title: Separate the two loops
variants.context: A HITL system runs two loops. The decision loop resolves the current case: the model predicts, a policy routes, and a person decides. The learning loop turns validated past decisions into a candidate model, so feedback crosses a quality gate before it can influence any future version.
variants.prompt: Labeling and retraining are paused for maintenance while traffic keeps arriving. Put what still happens to a case in order.

items.text: The routing policy still combines confidence, risk, and current review capacity.
The model returns a prediction with its uncertainty and version, because the synchronous path stays available.
The reviewer still decides the current case and records a rationale.
The validated-feedback gate holds the correction until the learning loop resumes.
The case still closes with owner, timestamps, and policy version recorded.

variants.hint: Which loop has a service-level objective attached to a single case?
variants.explanation: The decision loop must keep serving even when labeling or retraining is paused, which is why the two loops are deployed as separate services.

variants.title: Match the sampling source
variants.context: Active learning needs more than one source. Uncertainty samples sit near the current decision boundary, stratified samples preserve coverage across groups, random audit samples estimate performance on ordinary traffic, and user-reported cases surface severe failures without representing the population.
variants.prompt: Match each labeling source to what it contributes to the training set.

pairs.label: Uncertainty samples
pairs.detail: Expose cases sitting near the model's present decision boundary.

pairs.label: Stratified samples
pairs.detail: Preserve coverage across classes, regions, languages, devices, and risk groups.

pairs.label: Random audit samples
pairs.detail: Estimate performance on ordinary production traffic without routing bias.

pairs.label: User-reported cases
pairs.detail: Reveal severe product failures that no internal queue surfaced.

variants.hint: Ask what each source would miss if it were used alone.
variants.explanation: An uncertainty-only queue overrepresents the current boundary, so coverage, unbiased audits, and user reports are added to catch quiet failures.

variants.title: Match the sampling source
variants.context: Active learning needs more than one source. Uncertainty samples sit near the current decision boundary, stratified samples preserve coverage across groups, random audit samples estimate performance on ordinary traffic, and user-reported cases surface severe failures without representing the population.
variants.prompt: A team lists four goals for next quarter's labeling budget. Match each goal to the source that serves it.

pairs.label: Measure the true error rate on auto-decided traffic
pairs.detail: Draw a random audit sample that ignores the routing policy.

pairs.label: Stop a rare language from disappearing from the training set
pairs.detail: Impose quotas that keep every group represented.

pairs.label: Sharpen the boundary between two confusable classes
pairs.detail: Select the cases where the model is least certain.

pairs.label: Understand a severe complaint pattern from customers
pairs.detail: Pull the cases people escalated through the product.

variants.hint: Start from the question each goal asks, then pick the source that can answer it.
variants.explanation: Each source answers a different question, so a labeling budget spread across all four gives both boundary sharpness and honest coverage.

variants.title: Match the sampling source
variants.context: Active learning needs more than one source. Uncertainty samples sit near the current decision boundary, stratified samples preserve coverage across groups, random audit samples estimate performance on ordinary traffic, and user-reported cases surface severe failures without representing the population.
variants.prompt: Match each source to the bias it carries into the dataset when it is used alone.

pairs.label: Uncertainty only
pairs.detail: Overrepresents the boundary the deployed model already draws.

pairs.label: Stratified only
pairs.detail: Spends budget on easy cases just to hold group quotas.

pairs.label: Random audit only
pairs.detail: Needs a large sample before it says anything about rare classes.

pairs.label: User reports only
pairs.detail: Reflects who complains rather than who is affected.

variants.hint: Every source is a filter, and the filter shape becomes the dataset shape.
variants.explanation: Naive feedback is circular because the deployed model influences which cases people see, so sources are mixed to break that loop.

variants.title: Route the case
variants.context: Three patterns define where people add value. Exception review sends ambiguous or high-risk predictions to a general queue. Expert escalation sends policy-sensitive or unusually uncertain cases to qualified specialists. Active learning selects informative cases for labeling to improve a later model version.
variants.prompt: A claim is unusual, touches a regulated policy rule, and needs judgment the general queue is not trained or permitted to apply. Which path fits?
options: Active learning, because unusual cases are the most informative to label.
Exception review, because the case is ambiguous and the general queue is fastest.
Expert escalation, because the case is policy-sensitive and needs qualified reviewers.
optionFeedback: Active learning improves a later model; it does not resolve a live regulated decision.
The general queue lacks the permissions and training this decision requires.
Correct: policy-sensitive and unusually uncertain cases go to specialists with the right qualification.
variants.hint: Ask who is permitted and qualified to make this decision today.
variants.explanation: Expert escalation exists for policy-sensitive and unusually uncertain cases, and it has different latency, staffing, and evidence needs than general review.

variants.title: Route the case
variants.context: Three patterns define where people add value. Exception review sends ambiguous or high-risk predictions to a general queue. Expert escalation sends policy-sensitive or unusually uncertain cases to qualified specialists. Active learning selects informative cases for labeling to improve a later model version.
variants.prompt: A model auto-decides a large, low-risk category correctly most of the time. The team wants next quarter's model to be better there without adding live review. Which path fits?
options: Exception review, so a person confirms each auto-decision before it applies.
Expert escalation, so specialists set the correct answer for the category.
Active learning, selecting informative and representative cases for labeling.
optionFeedback: Adding live review to a low-risk high-volume category spends capacity without reducing harm.
Specialist capacity is scarce and this category carries no policy sensitivity.
Correct: the goal is a better later model, which is what informative sample selection is for.
variants.hint: Separate improving the next model from resolving today's case.
variants.explanation: Active learning has no service-level objective on the current case, so it can be batched and staffed differently from live review.

variants.title: Route the case
variants.context: Three patterns define where people add value. Exception review sends ambiguous or high-risk predictions to a general queue. Expert escalation sends policy-sensitive or unusually uncertain cases to qualified specialists. Active learning selects informative cases for labeling to improve a later model version.
variants.prompt: The expert queue is breaching deadlines while general review capacity sits idle. What should the routing policy do?
options: Raise the escalation threshold so fewer cases reach the experts at all.
Staff the expert queue separately and shed low-value labeling work first.
Move the overflow into the general queue so the deadlines stop breaching.
optionFeedback: That hides the problem by letting risky cases bypass the review they were routed for.
Correct: expert capacity is staffed on its own, and labeling work is shed before safety-critical review is delayed.
General reviewers lack the qualification, so the deadline is met by producing unqualified decisions.
variants.hint: Idle capacity is only useful if it is permitted to do the work.
variants.explanation: General review capacity cannot substitute for unavailable expertise, so expert queues are staffed separately and low-value work is shed first.

variants.title: Compute the operating metric
variants.context: HITL health is measured on several axes at once: review age by priority, reviewer agreement before adjudication, escaped errors that bypassed the intended review path, and cost per resolved case including review, escalation, quality control, and tooling.
variants.prompt: In one hour a queue resolves 400 cases. Review labor cost 120 dollars, escalations 40 dollars, quality control 20 dollars, and tooling 20 dollars. What is the cost per resolved case?
variants.hint: The metric counts every cost the review path incurs, not just the reviewers.
variants.explanation: Cost per resolved case totals review, escalation, quality control, and tooling, here 200 dollars over 400 cases.

mistakes.feedback: That counts review labor alone and leaves out escalation, quality control, and tooling.
That omits tooling, which the metric includes.

variants.title: Compute the operating metric
variants.context: HITL health is measured on several axes at once: review age by priority, reviewer agreement before adjudication, escaped errors that bypassed the intended review path, and cost per resolved case including review, escalation, quality control, and tooling.
variants.prompt: An audit of 5,000 auto-decided cases finds 180 errors that should have been routed for review. What is the escaped error rate?
variants.hint: Escaped errors are counted against the traffic that bypassed review.
variants.explanation: The escaped error rate is 180 of 5,000 expressed as a percentage, which is compared against the target of under 5 percent.

mistakes.feedback: That is the error count; the target is stated as a rate.
That is the proportion; the metric is reported in percent.

variants.title: Compute the operating metric
variants.context: HITL health is measured on several axes at once: review age by priority, reviewer agreement before adjudication, escaped errors that bypassed the intended review path, and cost per resolved case including review, escalation, quality control, and tooling.
variants.prompt: Two qualified reviewers independently label the same 400 cases and give the same answer on 332 of them. What is the raw agreement rate before adjudication?
variants.hint: Agreement is measured before any adjudication step resolves the disputes.
variants.explanation: Raw agreement is 332 of 400, which lands below the 85 percent bar and signals unclear guidance or an ambiguous label schema.

mistakes.feedback: That is the number of disagreements, not a rate.
That is the disagreement rate; the metric reports agreement.
